transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Conor Liu (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Veridian - Head of Security), Ethan Price (Platform Eng), Nadia Rivera (Compliance), Marco Silva (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery to map Redwood hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private) against Veridian's compliance controls. Goal: decide whether a hosted offering with additional controls is viable or if Private/VPC (on-prem style) is required. Action items: Redwood to share SOC2 artifacts + Private arch diagram; Veridian to share dataset/residency list.

Topics covered: SOC2 / ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC models, audit logging and SIEM, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM ownership, data retention policies, and tradeoffs by deployment mode.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:08] Laura (Veridian): Yep, loud and clear. Thanks, Maya.
[00:12] Maya: Great. I'll hand over to Conor in a sec to run the technical bits, but high-level — we're trying to map controls to your reqs. Can you start with current posture?
[00:23] Laura: Sure. So Veridian is in process of ISO 27001 readiness, and we have SOC2 Type II completed for our platform areas but we need any vendor access to be similarly auditable. We also have data residency rules for EU PII and APAC financials.
[00:36] Ethan (Veridian): To add, our infra team uses Okta for SSO, and we sync users via SCIM to downstream services. RBAC is enforced through groups in Okta tied to roles in our systems.
[00:47] Conor (Redwood): Ok, good to know. On Redwood's side, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user management for our Console, and RBAC with perms down to model/route level. There's a caveat — in hosted mode, audit logs and access metadata are available but the control plane is Redwood-managed.
[01:03] Nadia (Veridian): When you say "audit logs available" — what's the retention and can they stream to our SIEM? We need 12 months of immutable logs and integration into Splunk or SumoLogic.
[01:16] Conor: We can stream logs via syslog/HTTP forwarding to SIEM, and retention varies by plan. Dedicated and Private deployments give you longer retention and ability to control retention policies. For hosted, we provide configurable retention windows and export hooks; longer retention is available as an add-on. I should caveat: our hosted exports are eventually consistent and sometimes truncated in edge cases — there's a note in the doc.
[01:38] Marco (Veridian): That truncation bit — can you clarify? We need guaranteed completeness for audit trails for privileged ops.
[01:45] Conor: Right, good call. Hosted has best-effort streaming plus regular snapshots. If you need forensic-level guarantees, we recommend Dedicated with isolated log sinks or Private where you can own the log store.
[01:57] Laura: What about encryption? We have a requirement that keys for regulated data must be customer-managed KMS, and ideally HSM-backed.
[02:05] Maya: Redwood supports CMEK for Private and Dedicated; hosted supports CMEK for some enterprise tiers. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSMs via the KMS provider model. Note: sometimes product docs show limited coverage for embeddings and cache artifacts — Conor, can you explain?
[02:23] Conor: Yeah, worth calling out — in some older model runtimes, token cache metadata might be encrypted using platform keys; newer quantized runtimes support full CMEK. We have migration paths; we'll share a matrix mapping model variants to CMEK coverage.
[02:37] Ethan: Is there a way to keep KV cache off shared storage entirely in hosted?
[02:42] Conor: We do prefix/KV caching to drive cost and latency. In hosted, cache is multi-tenant but logically separated; Dedicated/Private gives you isolated cache nodes. If absolute isolation required, Private is the path.
[02:55] Laura: SSO — Okta SAML + SCIM is good. What about RBAC granularity? Can we map Okta groups to per-model access?
[03:02] Conor: Yes, you can map SCIM groups to RBAC roles and then to per-model and per-route permissions. One caveat: older Console UIs show role names slightly differently in logs — sometimes labeled as "RedwoodRole" in the event stream; it's cosmetic but sometimes confusing.
[03:16] Nadia: About compliance evidence: we'll need an arranger of docs — SOC2 report, ISO cert, pen test summaries. Do you publish any redacted pen test results?
[03:26] Maya: We can provide a SOC2 Type II report and a redacted pentest summary. We also publish an architecture security whitepaper. We'll include links in the follow-up email.
[03:35] Laura: Will that include Private deployment diagrams? I want to see control plane data flows when the control plane is customer-managed.
[03:42] Conor: Yes — for Private we have a diagram showing the private control plane, option for air-gapped on-prem or VPC peering. Important note: some customers run a hybrid where control plane is customer-managed but inference nodes remain in cloud regions. We'll highlight the differences.
[03:58] Ethan: For VPC peering, what network requirements? NAT, routing, and port rules? We have tight egress controls.
[04:05] Conor: We require outbound TLS to a narrow set of endpoints for telemetry and control. For Private you can disable outbound telemetry entirely and use an on-prem control plane. We'll share the egress whitelist.
[04:16] Marco: And auditability — if control plane is customer-managed, do logs live with us?
[04:20] Conor: Yes, in Private the control plane logs are in your environment; in Dedicated we can deliver logs to your sinks; in hosted we provide export APIs and scheduled raw logs.
[04:30] Laura: How do you handle data residency for embeddings? We ingest text and build embeddings; are those stored in region X if we request EU-only?
[04:38] Maya: You can pin model instances and storage to regions. For EU-only datasets we'll recommend Dedicated or Private to guarantee residency. Hosted supports region pinning but some cache layers may be global unless configured. We'll send the exact gating matrix.
[04:54] Nadia: Who holds the keys in the CMEK model? Is it always customer KMS or do you support split custody?
[05:00] Conor: Primary mode is customer-managed keys (you own the KMS). We also support bring-your-own-HSM for Private. Split custody (multi-party keys) is supported with partners but requires additional integration; we'll note that in the follow-up.
[05:14] Laura: How do you prevent model outputs or prompt logs from being retained longer than our retention policy?
[05:20] Maya: We have configurable retention on prompt/response logs per-route and per-tenant in Dedicated/Private; hosted supports per-tenant retention but with minimum windows. For strict legal needs, Private gives you full control.
[05:31] Ethan: Any SOC or infra automation we can integrate? Like periodic compliance exports?
[05:36] Conor: We expose APIs for export of audit data and support scheduled S3 exports for backups and archives. We also integrate with SIEMs for alerting; sample dashboards for Datadog/Splunk exist.
[05:48] Marco: Regarding SAML — do you support assertion encryption or just signing?
[05:52] Conor: We support signed assertions and can enable encrypted assertions upon request. SCIM supports incremental provisioning and deprovisioning events.
[06:01] Laura: What about privileged access reviews and RBAC attestation?
[06:05] Maya: We have audit reports that can show admin changes, role grants, and login events for attestation. For Dedicated/Private you can also plug audit logs into your identity governance tools.
[06:16] Nadia: Pen tests — are red team results available? We require a summary including severity and remediation timelines.
[06:23] Maya: We can share a redacted executive summary and timeline for critical findings. Full reports are under NDA in most cases.
[06:31] Conor: One operational thing — the runtime uses continuous batching and KV caches; in older runtimes we had a small leakage window for ephemeral cache writes — it's been largely mitigated but good to call out for strict handling.
[06:46] Ethan: That leakage window — how long and does it affect embeddings storage?
[06:50] Conor: Typically sub-second to a few seconds for in-memory caches; persistent stores are encrypted and subject to retention. We'll include the cache TTLs and eviction policy in the appendix.
[07:02] Laura: Any customers in our vertical using Private?
[07:06] Maya: Yes, at least two financial services customers and a healthcare SaaS vendor. We can provide references under NDA.
[07:13] Laura: Ok — that helps. On governance, do you support SSO enforced MFA and adaptive auth?
[07:20] Conor: We integrate with IdPs that enforce MFA; Redwood respects the SAML assertions. Adaptive auth typically lives on Okta/GCP side.
[07:27] Marco: For incident response — how do we get notified of security incidents that potentially touch our data?
[07:32] Maya: We have an incident response SLA and notification process for potential data exposures. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer tighter RTO/RPO and custom IR runbooks. We'll share an IR playbook excerpt.
[07:44] Nadia: Are you certified ISO 27001?
[07:47] Maya: We're in final stages of ISO 27001 certification — we'll share the cert status and evidence in follow-up.
[07:53] Laura: Ok, final one from me — what's the recommended path if our legal wants full control of keys and retention but we also want Redwood-managed updates?
[08:01] Conor: Common pattern is Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and an opt-in for Redwood to operate the runtime under an SLA, with all logs shipped to your SIEM. Alternatively Private with a customer control plane gives you the most control but more ops overhead. We'll put a comparison matrix in the follow-up.
[08:18] Maya: Great. I think we've captured the major requirements. Quick recap and next steps?
[08:23] Laura: Veridian will compile the list of regulated datasets and residency rules; we want SOC2 artifacts and Private arch diagram.
[08:31] Maya: Perfect. We'll send the SOC2, pen test executive summary, and the control plane diagram. Also Conor will add the runtime/CMEK coverage matrix and the cache TTL appendix.
[08:45] Conor: I'll also assemble sample IAM role mappings and an example SCIM group-to-role mapping.
[08:51] Maya: Thanks all. We'll aim to get those docs in the next 3–7 days and follow up to schedule the infra deep-dive with Marco and Ethan.
[08:59] Laura: Thanks — appreciate it.

End of transcript.
